A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated that a pipelined-SAS ADC with open-loop integrators can be used to support a very high sampling rate (4GS/s) and resolution (13b) in a small area (1.2 mm2) with a reasonable power consumption (1.2mW).

we have designed a 13b 3.5GS/s 2-channel ADC in a 65nm CMOS process, with a 4GS/s channel sampling rate and 3.3mW/channel power consumption, which is the highest reported sampling speed for a SAR ADC with 10b resolution.

a three-stage asynchronous ADC with 13-bit resolution and 4GS/s sampling rate was fabricated in a 65nm CMOS process, achieving an FOM of 0.4fJ/conv. step and a linearity of -70.2dBFS THD at 100MHz input frequency.
The main takeaway from our work is that

dynamic pipelined ADC architectures with open-loop amplifiers can be made to work at high speed, with good linearity, and without calibration, if the dynamic circuits and calibration loops are properly designed.
